### The check

On a Node.js server start, `register()` in [src/instrumentation.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b96fde4-d1d5-4c39-bf28-3cee23b32899/src/instrumentation.ts) registers event handlers and starts the scheduler. `startScheduler()` in [src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b96fde4-d1d5-4c39-bf28-3cee23b32899/src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts) sets a timer that calls `tick()` every minute. The overdue job’s cadence is 60 minutes; `tick()` enqueues it when due, then drains the queue. `runHandler()` in [src/server/jobs/queue.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b96fde4-d1d5-4c39-bf28-3cee23b32899/src/server/jobs/queue.ts) dispatches that queued job to `runOverdueIssueJob()`.

There is also a protected trigger: `POST` in [src/app/api/cron/overdue/route.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b96fde4-d1d5-4c39-bf28-3cee23b32899/src/app/api/cron/overdue/route.ts) checks the cron secret and calls the same runner directly.

`runOverdueIssueJob()` in [src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b96fde4-d1d5-4c39-bf28-3cee23b32899/src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts) first checks the archived-issue scope, then gets up to 50 organization IDs from `listOrgIdsForRollup()` in [src/server/repositories/usage-repository.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b96fde4-d1d5-4c39-bf28-3cee23b32899/src/server/repositories/usage-repository.ts). For each organization, `listOverdueIssues()` in [src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b96fde4-d1d5-4c39-bf28-3cee23b32899/src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts) selects live issues in that organization with a non-null due date strictly before the scan time and a status of `backlog`, `todo`, `in_progress`, or `in_review`. Closed, archived, undated, and not-yet-due issues are excluded.

### Event, deduplication, and alert

For each selected issue, the job skips a null due date and checks the module-level `reported` set by issue ID. If it has not been seen, the job emits `issue.overdue` with the organization, issue, due date, and assignee IDs. The job’s responsibility ends at scanning, suppressing repeats, and publishing that fact; it does not build notification rows or send mail.

The set prevents another announcement on later scans in the same server process. The job adds the ID after `emit()` completes. This is process-memory state, not a persisted delivery record, so it does not survive a process restart. The event bus’s `emit()` in [src/lib/event-bus.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b96fde4-d1d5-4c39-bf28-3cee23b32899/src/lib/event-bus.ts) waits for subscribers and isolates their failures; consequently, the job’s set is not a durable guarantee that every subscriber successfully delivered an alert.

At startup, importing [src/server/services/event-registry.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b96fde4-d1d5-4c39-bf28-3cee23b32899/src/server/services/event-registry.ts) also imports [src/server/services/notification-service.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b96fde4-d1d5-4c39-bf28-3cee23b32899/src/server/services/notification-service.ts), which subscribes to `issue.overdue`. Its handler skips an unassigned issue; otherwise it calls `notify()` for the single `assigneeId`, with the overdue title, body, and issue link. `notify()` looks up that recipient’s `issue_overdue` preference and `resolveChannels()` computes the row’s channel list. Without a saved preference, the default is `in_app` and `email`. Preferences are edited through `NotificationPreferencesForm` in [src/components/domain/notification/notification-preferences-form.tsx](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b96fde4-d1d5-4c39-bf28-3cee23b32899/src/components/domain/notification/notification-preferences-form.tsx), submitted via `updateNotificationPreferenceAction()` in [src/actions/notifications/update-preferences.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b96fde4-d1d5-4c39-bf28-3cee23b32899/src/actions/notifications/update-preferences.ts), and stored by `upsertPreference()` in [src/server/repositories/notification-preference-repository.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b96fde4-d1d5-4c39-bf28-3cee23b32899/src/server/repositories/notification-preference-repository.ts).

`notify()` inserts the notification row through `insertNotifications()` in [src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b96fde4-d1d5-4c39-bf28-3cee23b32899/src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts), including the computed channels. The in-app panel loads rows for the signed-in user through `listNotifications()` in the notification service and repository.

One delivery detail in the current code: channel selection is stored with the row, but it is not fully enforced by delivery. The in-app listing does not filter on the `in_app` channel, and the overdue fan-out does not call an email sender. Email is sent by the separate `runDigestEmailJob()` in [src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b96fde4-d1d5-4c39-bf28-3cee23b32899/src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts): for an eligible organization at its configured UTC digest hour, it builds a digest for digest subscribers, sends it through `sendEmail()`, and marks included rows read. So an overdue row may appear in that digest, but selecting email alone does not cause an immediate overdue email in this path.
